newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE sees Chechnya peace unchanged by Lebed move.
newsitem.headline: OSCE sees Chechnya peace unchanged by Lebed move.

text.p: The sacking of Russian security chief Alexander Lebed, architect of Russia's recent peace deal in Chechnya, should not affect the peace process, the head of an international mediating mission there said on Friday.

Swiss diplomat Tim Guldimann, who leads the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) assistance group to the rebel Russian province, told Reuters in a telephone interview he was optimistic that progress would continue.
"I do not interpret it as a changing attitude of the Russian government with regard to Chechnya", he said.

Russia on Friday announced Lebed would lose his role as chief peace negotiator in Chechnya. "Lebed's dismissal as the presidential envoy to Chechnya is a matter of time," Yeltsin's spokesman, Sergei Yastrzhembsky, said by telephone in Moscow. "New candidates for the job are being discussed now."

"The peace process is fragile and this is a new element that doesn't make it easier for the immediate steps to be followed," said Guldimann. But he added he was pleased Lebed would continue to work for peace in the breakaway province.

Lebed won acclaim abroad for his part in reaching an agreement with separatists in August to postpone the issue of Chechnya's political status for five years, in return for a withdrawal of Russian troops from the region.
Lebed, who on Friday announced plans to stand for president in forthcoming elections, has come under fire from Russian parliamentarians for ceding too much to the rebels.
Asked if Lebed's demotion was likely to harm the cause of the Chechen side, Guldimann answered: "Not necessarily. We have to see".
